data.content_ref: inline:The target's core move is to characterize preference for the better-corroborated theory as a 'rational guess toward truth' rather than an 'expectation of future success,' thereby claiming to avoid induction. But this distinction is structurally inert: both a 'guess' and an 'expectation' select the same theory for the same reason — because it has survived more severe tests in the past. The target's own mechanism states scientists prefer the better-corroborated theory 'because it is the most informative and least refuted map available.' 'Least refuted' is a purely retrospective property. For it to function as a reason for preference — to make the guess 'rational' rather than arbitrary — the agent must bridge past survival to present preference. That bridge is exactly the inductive inference the target disclaims. If the guess does not use past test-survival as its warrant, it is indistinguishable from a coin flip and the word 'rational' does no work. If it does use past test-survival, the inference is inductive regardless of whether it is labeled 'guess' or 'expectation.' The target has stripped away justification (rejected by Popper), probabilistic expectation (explicitly disclaimed), and any guarantee of future performance (conceded as the 'cost'), leaving 'preference' with no remaining normative basis that is not either vacuous or covertly inductive. The relabeling of inductive structure as 'critical preference' does not change its logical form; it merely hides it.
